episodes.notes: Chronological five-part scientific biography of Roger Wolcott Sperry (1913–1994), Michael S. Gazzaniga (b. 1939), and Francis Crick's (1916–2004) twenty-eight-year final quest alongside Christof Koch (b. 1956) to transform human consciousness into an experimental neurobiological science. Traces Sperry's refutation of Paul Weiss's neural resonance dogma via rat nerve-crosses and 180-degree amphibian eye rotations leading to the 1963 Chemoaffinity Hypothesis; Myers, Bogen, Sperry, and Gazzaniga's split-brain investigations on commissurotomy patients W.J., N.G., L.B., and P.S., culminating in Gazzaniga and LeDoux's discovery of the confabulating Left-Hemisphere Interpreter; Crick's 1976 move to the Salk Institute, the 1990–2003 Neural Correlates of Consciousness program, Logothetis's macaque binocular rivalry recordings, and Crick's July 28, 2004 hospital-bed revisions on the claustrum tested against modern single-axon 3D reconstructions and central thalamic stimulation. Concludes at one-Angstrom scale inside the EphA4–ephrin-A5 ectodomain complex (PDB 4M4R) and the human alpha1-beta3-gamma2L GABA-A receptor (PDB 6HUP).

episodes.notes: After winning the 1972 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine at age forty-three for solving the covalent chemical structure of antibodies (covered in Episode 2427), former concert-caliber violinist Gerald M. Edelman (1929–2014) walked away from immunology at its peak to spend forty-two fearless years asking how an unlabeled embryo builds a conscious brain. Tracing his second career chronologically from Rockefeller University to his bespoke La Jolla 'scientific monastery' at The Neurosciences Institute, this deep dive explores his purification of the first vertebrate cell-adhesion molecules (NCAM and L-CAM), Topobiology, Neural Darwinism (the Theory of Neuronal Group Selection), reentrant cortical signaling solving the binding problem like a conductorless string quartet, biological degeneracy, primary consciousness as 'the remembered present,' physical Brain-Based Devices (Darwin I through Nomad), and the Dynamic Core Hypothesis forged with Giulio Tononi. The atomic finale steps inside the 2.00-Angstrom crystal structure of NCAM Ig1-Ig2-Ig3 (PDB 1QZ1) to reveal how immunoglobulin-superfamily double zippers and polysialic acid sculpt synapses—and how TMS-EEG complexity today detects covert consciousness at the ICU bedside.

episodes.label: Ibn al-Nafis & Michael Servetus (1213–1288 / 1511–1553) — Demolishing Galen's Invisible Septal Pores: Cairo's 1242 Anatomy Commentary, Paris Dissections Alongside Vesalius, Christianismi Restitutio's Hidden Pulmonary-Transit Pages, and the Green-Oak Pyre in Geneva
episodes.notes: Long before William Harvey's 1628 De Motu Cordis closed the systemic vascular loop, who first demolished Galen's thirteen-hundred-year dogma of invisible pores in the interventricular septum and discovered the pulmonary transit of blood through the lungs? This chronological historical and biophysical deep dive pairs two extraordinary rebels separated by three centuries: thirteenth-century Syrian jurist-physician Ibn al-Nafis (1213–1288), writing his 1242 Commentary on Anatomy in Avicenna's Canon in Cairo, and sixteenth-century Aragonese polymath Miguel Serveto—Michael Servetus (1511–1553)—dissecting human cadavers alongside Andreas Vesalius in Paris before hiding Europe's first printed account of pulmonary oxygenation inside pages 169–171 of his forbidden 1553 treatise Christianismi Restitutio. Tracing the Mediterranean manuscript bridge of Venetian Damascus doctor Andrea Alpago, the green-oak pyre at Champel in Geneva, only three surviving octavos on Earth, and Muhyo al-Deen al-Tatawi's 1924 Berlin rediscovery, the finale shrinks to one Angstrom inside 1.25-Angstrom X-ray structures of human deoxyhemoglobin (PDB 2DN2) and oxyhemoglobin (PDB 2DN1) to resolve how sub-Angstrom iron-spin flattening turns dark venous blood crimson across the lung.

episodes.label: William Harvey (1578–1657) — Padua's Anatomy Theater, Venous Valves, the 1628 Stroke-Volume Proof, and Civil-War Exile
episodes.notes: From Elizabethan Folkestone and the dark walnut galleries of Padua's 1594 anatomical theater to twelve cautious years of eel vivisections and forearm ligatures at St. Bartholomew's Hospital, follow short, dagger-wearing royal physician William Harvey as he unleashes the 1628 Frankfurt quarto De Motu Cordis and its devastating Chapter IX stroke-volume proof—surviving a collapsed London practice, exonerating the 1634 Lancashire witches, reading calmly beneath a hedge as cannonballs strike at Edgehill, enduring the Parliamentary burning of his Whitehall manuscripts, answering Paris's Jean Riolan, and leaving one missing microscopic link closed four years after his death by Marcello Malpighi's 1661 frog-lung lens, followed by a One-Ångström molecular epilogue inside deoxyhemoglobin (PDB 2HHB) and oxyhemoglobin (PDB 1HHO).
